title: I Enforced the Racquetball Court Clock on the Duo Who Booked Ghost Slots

parts.text: I waited outside court B at 6:00 p.m. with a reservation that said 6:00. The duo inside had booked 5:00, 5:30, and 6:00 under three fake names. The club clock policy they had complained into existence said: ONE SLOT PER MEMBER. GHOST NAMES BAN THE CARD. I was thirty-seven, night player, holding my real barcode. They yelled, "We're in a run." I pointed at the clock. They served. I photographed the three names, the policy email, and the clock. Then I asked the front desk to run the barcodes. At 6:04 the desk asked why two cards owned three ghost slots.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see three names on one run against the ghost-name ban they wanted.

social.video_title: They ghost-booked three slots for one run — Part 1/2
social.description: 6:00 barcode, a run behind glass, and a policy they demanded. I ran the cards. Would you have stretched in the hall?

parts.text: They called it a glitch until the names matched two emails. I printed the ticket, the email, and the photo. Court B opened. Their cards sat 48 hours. They told the league the policy was always about optics. Optics is a word duos use when a barcode exists. Clock policy now has a second line: RUNS ARE NOT THREE NAMES. I play B. They book one. The glass finally shows a fair game.

social.video_title: Runs are not three ghost names — Part 2/2
social.description: Ghost-slot ticket, a 48-hour sit, and a second line on the clock. Was a run ever a fake roster?
